correctness.rationale: The mathematical finding is unchanged. A middle singleton or any nonsingleton covers both extreme rows; sole extreme-row vertices cover just their own extreme. Hence a triple suffices exactly when its two extreme-coverage bits have union 3. The pair-state trace counts the labeled cyclic configurations with their multiplicative weights (including n=3 with three distinct columns). Recomputing the characteristic polynomial over Z[u,v,X] using destination-symbol weights gives X^7 A B. At z=-1 its nonzero factor is (X−1)^3(X+1)^2(X²+1)^2, which gives 9 on multiples of four and 1 otherwise. The repair removes the erroneous orientation argument in the frozen prior-work comparison. By commutativity of the strong product, the relevant Table 2 row is n=3 (path length), whose signed values conflict with independent direct enumeration under the specified graph definition; the revision states the discrepancy and includes an elementary circumference-three check.
residual_risks: The reason for the published Table 2 discrepancy is not established. The explicit closed-neighborhood definition and transfer proof, not that table, certify the claimed family.
